metadata.title: POA&M: sample-gcp, SC-28 + SC-28(1)
metadata.remarks: Created by automation/ar2poam.py from the step 6 assessment results; its two drafts (sc-28_obj and sc-28.1_obj-2, one cause) were merged into one risk and one item, as in the sample-azure POA&M. The observations and findings are copies from those results (same uuids). Decision: accept the risk (deviation requested). Ratings, dates and owner are placeholders to review. When an authorising official approves, set the risk status to deviation-approved and the response lifecycle to completed.

poam-items.title: Accept the risk: Firestore data is not tamper-evident (SC-28(1) obj-2)
poam-items.description: The (default) Firestore database has no cryptographic tamper evidence, so sc-28.1_obj-2 and the integrity part of sc-28_obj are not satisfied. Disposition: risk acceptance (deviation requested); see the related risk.

risks.title: Unauthorized modification of Firestore data would go undetected
risks.description: The (default) Firestore database has no cryptographic tamper evidence, and nothing outside it records what the demoItems data should be. An identity that bypasses the security rules (the project owner, or the github-deploy service account with roles/datastore.owner) could change stored data without it being detectable. Confidentiality at rest is not affected: Firestore encrypts all stored data.
risks.statement: If stored application data is modified without authorisation, the change cannot be detected or proven, so the integrity of the data cannot be relied on (SC-28 integrity, SC-28(1) obj-2).

mitigating-factors.description: firestore.rules deny every update and delete from clients and allow only the creation of the three seed documents with fixed values. Only identities that bypass the rules can modify the data: the project owner and the github-deploy service account (roles/datastore.owner).

remediations.title: Accept the risk (deviation)
remediations.description: Accept that sc-28.1_obj-2, and the integrity part of sc-28_obj, stay not satisfied for sample-gcp. Justification: clients cannot modify the data (firestore.rules deny every update and delete and allow only the creation of the three fixed seed documents), so exposure is limited to the privileged identities, and the data is public, non-sensitive demonstration data. Alternatives considered and not chosen: a digest of the known contents verified regularly (only holds while the data is fixed, and needs adapter support); server-side writes with an application hash chain (adds a server tier the sample avoids); moving to a datastore with built-in tamper evidence (none identified on GCP; changes the architecture). Revisit if the data becomes writable or sensitive.

tasks.title: Risk acceptance approved

tasks.title: Annual review of the acceptance
tasks.description: Re-assess the risk (run automation/run_assessment.py gcp) and renew, revise or replace the acceptance, in particular if the demoItems data becomes writable or sensitive.
